fact_check.claim: '57% of the S&P 500 companies are now more volatile than Bitcoin... as Grayscale just said' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified and current. Grayscale Research, 'Putting Bitcoin's Volatility in Context', released October 14, 2026: Bitcoin's one-year realized volatility is 43%, lower than 57% of individual S&P 500 companies (down from 81% five years ago, under the 10-year average of 64%). A few outlets print 19%; the Crypto Briefing write-up of the report confirms 57%. Copy uses 57% and 43%.

fact_check.claim: 'It closed for the week... below the May high, which isn't too bad because it's so far up from the 50 week moving average... we're using a 50-day moving average as support, almost a week and a half' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified. Sunday October 18 close about $82,002 (Friday $81,501); the May 2026 high is about $82.8K (verified in the downtober ledger); the 50-week SMA is about $76.1K (CoinCodex, October 19) to $78.8K (FXStreet at the September 21 reclaim), so copy says 'roughly $76K to $79K'; the 50-day SMA is about $81.7K (Investing.com, October 19) with price about $82K to $82.8K, consistent with 'riding the 50-day SMA for about a week and a half' (kept as Mike's chart read, no exact day count claimed). Copy: 'closed the week just under the May high at about $82K, still well above the 50-week SMA'.

fact_check.claim: 'last week when we had the horrible PPI reading Bitcoin went down for two hours and then went all the way back up... made it a green candle' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified in the was-i-right ledger (October 15 PPI 6.3% y/y, intraday low about $79,800, rebound to $82K to $83K, green close). Copy says 'on the hot PPI print this month' to avoid a stale week reference.

fact_check.claim: 'I don't understand how everybody thinks that we're not going to get a rate hike in the end of October... the market is pricing in a pause' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified and current. CME FedWatch October 18: 84.5% hold at 3.75% to 4.00%, 15.5% for a 25 bp hike at the October 27-28 FOMC (a hike spiked to about 42% intraday on the October 14 CPI, then faded after Chair Warsh declined to prejudge). Copy says '84% pause priced' and 'October 28'. The hike-unless-a-war-ends read is Mike's own and is written as his.

fact_check.claim: 'Anthropic... committing a portion of Anthropic's shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund... start off with 5% of our shares... every 50% increase in the company's value... an extra 2%' (transcript, read off the post)
fact_check.verdict: verified. Announced Sunday October 18, 2026: 5% of shares to a new wholly owned Public Benefit Fund, subject to shareholder approval; the board may add 2 percentage points for each 50% increase in value above an undisclosed baseline; labor-market disruption from AI is among the causes it may address; no lobbying or political donations. Copy: 'pledged 5% of its shares... aimed partly at AI job disruption', '2 more points for every 50% jump'.

fact_check.claim: Musk interview played on stream: 'Money won't matter in 2036... the Treasury should just simply issue people checks... deflation will be the issue, not inflation' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified. From Musk's taped interview with The Economist's editor-in-chief Zanny Minton Beddoes, released July 23, 2026: money won't matter by 2036 because robots and AI will out-produce consumption; the Treasury should issue direct payments; if output grows faster than the money supply, deflation, not inflation, is the issue. Copy attributes it to 'The Economist this summer'. Mike's 'the Trump feud was fake' read is a political tangent (persona avoid_in_drafts) and is NOT drafted.

fact_check.claim: 'We ask Claude what Bitcoin and Solana could be by 2030... Bitcoin would reach 240,000 and Solana 320 by 2030' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified. 24/7 Wall St, October 19, 2026: Claude's base case is $240,000 Bitcoin and $320 Solana by the end of 2030 (ranges $150K to $400K and $70 to $700) from about $82,810 and $106. Copy uses $240K and $320; 'sounds low, especially Solana' is Mike's take.

fact_check.claim: Kaspa price (stated only as 'Kaspa and TAO, lots of multipliers' on stream; copy needs the level)
fact_check.verdict: current: about $0.036 (Bybit October 17, market cap about $1.01B), about 83% under the $0.207 all-time high. Copy says 'under 4 cents' and 'about 3.6 cents'.

fact_check.claim: Bittensor / TAO (named on stream only as the multiplier play; copy adds the current catalyst and price)
fact_check.verdict: verified. Null Consensus is an opt-in subnet scoring mode that raises per-subnet capacity from 256 to 2,500 identifiers (new subnets stay on Yuma by default); TAO jumped more than 10% to above $285 on October 16 on the announcement, then settled near $260 to $276 (Coinbase about $268.58, OKX $275.9 on October 17). Release-date reporting conflicts (Runtime 475 on October 7 vs 'upcoming' on bittensor.com), so copy says 'just unveiled' and quotes no release date. Copy: '256 slots to 2,500', 'popped above $285... settling near $270'.

fact_check.claim: 'Arb, Arbitrum is a good one. The tech Robinhood uses... it's in that tokenized assets narrative' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified. Robinhood Chain is an Ethereum L2 built on the Arbitrum Orbit (Nitro) stack, mainnet live July 1, 2026, chain id 4663, built for tokenized stocks (ERC-20 Stock Tokens). Copy: 'Robinhood Chain is built on Arbitrum tech'. No price or multiplier claim.

fact_check.claim: 'Litecoin is roughly the same market cap of Sui, just a few hundred million more than Sui... Litecoin already have an ETF... considered a privacy coin now, optional privacy... Sui has VCs and backing' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified. Litecoin market cap about $4.6B vs Sui about $4.1B (Coinbase / OKX / Bybit, October 19-20). The Canary spot Litecoin ETF (LTCC) is trading on Nasdaq; MWEB opt-in confidential transactions have been live since 2022 (Litecoin's 15-year anniversary was October 2026). Sui is VC backed with ongoing unlocks. Copy uses 'about $4.6B vs about $4.1B', 'a spot ETF already trading', 'optional privacy', 'no insider unlocks' vs 'VC backed'. 'Made in America token' and the 'Litecoin all-time high market cap 23 billion' figure are not verified and not used.

fact_check.claim: 'JPMorgan is set to sell off... 165 billion US stocks, they're dumping AI stocks as concerns grow' (transcript, read off a post)
fact_check.verdict: NOT verified as described, dropped. The $165B figure is JPMorgan's June 2026 quarter-end REBALANCING estimate (pensions, sovereign funds), not a JPMorgan AI-stock dump and not an October event; the AI-bubble warning is a separate, older Jason Hunter note. No content drafted.

fact_check.claim: 'We're getting QE. It's not much of it... five billion' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: NOT verified, dropped. The New York Fed has paused reserve-management bill purchases for a third straight month (reinvesting $14.6B of maturities only; purchases expected to resume mid-November), and no $5B figure appears in current reporting. No QE claim drafted.

fact_check.claim: 'Putin calling for a summit with Trump and Xi... to end the Ukraine war... Zelensky was not invited' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: NOT verified for October 2026 (the 'Zelensky not invited' framing traces to August 2025 coverage; the latest verified Ukraine talks are the September 24 Trump-Xi White House meeting). Copy keeps Mike's condition general: 'unless a war ends'. No summit content drafted.

fact_check.claim: 'the four-year cycle zombies, they front-run the October bottom. They push us all the way up into a bull market in the end of September, like I was saying for the whole year... now the market is crap... volume went up in September, now it's just going down' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: Mike's own thesis (persona core_theses: the self-defeating October bottom), consistent with the verified September rebound (about 45% off the June 30 low to about $85K to $87K by late September, in the was-i-right and downtober ledgers). Written as his call; per the drafting rule it says the zombies front-ran the bottom and pushed price up, never that they caused an October bottom. The sliding-volume read is his statement.

fact_check.claim: 'software engineers don't really need to do anything but review code... bottlenecking on the code review process... now they're creating agents' / 'biggest economic expansion that humanity has ever seen' / 'everything is going to be so damn cheap' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: Mike's own observations and forecasts, written as his view (first person), no external statistic attached.

fact_check.claim: Community track record and private plays: MYX 550x, DNR 137x, LAB 350x, Velvet 58x, Disco 47x, Pippin, Peak, Banker, Morpho +130%, Pepe +83%, 'mellow man' / 'mad fury' 7x, 'two coma Inu', ZBCN (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: membership-pitch and micro-cap material (the lane 3 brief skips membership pitches; most names are unverifiable chat reads). Not researched, no content drafted; 'degen plays are dead, long-term plays only' is kept as Mike's general stance.

fact_check.claim: Musk-Trump 'fake feud' theory, socialism / IQ / birth-rate tangent, Trump accounts, 'New Mexico to New America', Back to the Future parody, flying-car videos, 'worst housing market in history' post, 'Iran war' resolution (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: political and personal tangents (persona avoid_in_drafts), skipped. Mike can post these himself.

fact_check.claim: 'ETH is probably one of the best to go with in terms of safety... ETH is going to steal the show' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: Mike's opinion; not drafted (persona: never put ETH in favorites / stacking framing). ETH is left out of copy entirely.

fact_check.claim: Zcash check
fact_check.verdict: no 'Zcash' or 'zcash' in this transcript; nothing to resolve.

yt_posts.body:
AI is taking the jobs. Invest while you still have the paycheck.

Software engineers at the big companies are barely writing code anymore; they review what the AI wrote, and the bottleneck moved to code review. Now they are building agents to do the review too. The bottleneck is gone, and it is heading down the line into robotics next.

Here is the part nobody wants to say out loud.

Think about the horseless carriage. First it was a curious news story. A couple of years later there were tens of thousands of them. A couple of years after that, hundreds of thousands, everywhere. Robotics is on that exact curve, and those machines can do pretty much any job.

For all of history there was a relationship between governments, businesses and the people, because no matter how badly they were treated, somebody had to do the work. That has never not been true. Now, for the first time, labor is about to stop being needed.

You can already see the big players positioning for it. Anthropic, on October 18, pledged 5% of its shares to a new Public Benefit Fund, with 2 more points for every 50% jump in the company's value, and labor-market disruption from AI is one of the things it is meant to address. Elon Musk told The Economist this summer that money won't matter by 2036, that the Treasury should just issue people checks, and that deflation, not inflation, will be the problem, because output will grow faster than the money supply.

Call it what you want. My point is simpler: everything is going to get very cheap, and assets are going to get very expensive. I think we are walking into the biggest economic expansion humanity has ever seen. Not the last hundred years. Ever.

So you invest while you can, while the paycheck is still landing.

And you own the things nobody can print and nobody can own. Governments and corporations are racing to control compute, money and AI infrastructure, and the more they race, the more valuable the neutral layers get: Bittensor ($TAO) as the AI inference layer, Kaspa ($KAS) as the proof-of-work money layer. Two sides of the same principle, and both still far under their all-time highs.

When the robots take the labor, which hits first: deflation (Musk's call) or inflation (the printer)? Pick one in the comments, and tell me what you are stacking with the paychecks you have left.

yt_posts.body:
57% of S&P 500 companies are now more volatile than Bitcoin. And $BTC still closed the week just under the May high, with the October 28 Fed decision coming.

Here is the setup as I see it, and exactly where I buy everything.

Start with the Grayscale report this week: Bitcoin's one-year realized volatility is down to 43%, lower than 57% of the individual S&P 500 names. That is resilience. On the hot PPI print this month Bitcoin dipped for about two hours, got bought straight back up, and closed the candle green.

The chart: $BTC closed the week at about $82K, just under the May high of about $82.8K, still well above the 50-week SMA (roughly $76K to $79K depending on who you ask), and it has been riding the 50-day SMA as support for about a week and a half. Not bad. Not a breakout either.

Everything has played out the way I said all year. The four-year cycle zombies front-ran the prophesied October bottom and pushed us up into the end of September. Now volume is sliding, the board is red, and the degen plays are dead. Long-term plays only from here; that is all I am adding.

Now the Fed. On October 28 the market prices an 84% chance of a pause. I see a hike. What would stop it? A war ending, maybe. Nothing else on the table. And because everybody is pricing a pause, nobody is pricing the hike, which is exactly how you get the down, down, down.

So my plan is simple. Unless something big happens, we are probably due for a monster dump into the end of October. If Bitcoin tumbles under the 50-week SMA, that is the moment I buy everything on my list. Until then, small DCA buys here and there, because there is always a chance it does not happen, and you cannot buy the bottom you are waiting for if it never prints.

And when it comes to what I buy: if you want relative safety with lots of multipliers, it is still Kaspa ($KAS) and Bittensor ($TAO). Both far under their all-time highs, both chains that nobody owns.

Does Bitcoin lose the 50-week SMA before October ends, or do the zombies hold the floor again? Pick one, and tell me what you buy if it does.
